value.account:
WHAT I CHANGED
- New pure auditor orchestrator/workflow/resume_projection_integrity.py (ResumeScopePath, audit_scope, ResumeProjectionIntegrityError, plus reached-call helpers) with resume_call_lineage.py (index_retry_lineage, next_unused_retry_frame_id, CallFrameRetryLineageError), resume_loop_progress.py (for_each / four repeat_until forms, ResumeProjectionValidationError) and resume_root_checksum.py. Project-wide module-level name audit_scope is imported in cli/commands/resume.py, workflow/executor.py and workflow/calls.py.
- state_projection.py: CallBoundaryProjection.import_alias, ResumeSlot / ResumeProjectionSlotIndex / resolutions, enumerate_resume_slots, resolve_resume_step_id, resolve_call_boundary. Loop iteration ranges come from the state (for_each items) or a new WorkflowStateProjection.repeat_until_max_iterations map (kept off IterationStepKeyProjection so structural goldens only gain import_alias). lowering.py populates both.
- CLI resume: load + existing checksum precheck, then audit, then observability override write, session, process metadata, executor. Observability write moved after the checks so a rejected resume writes nothing. A failing session close no longer replaces the result.
- Executor: structural-root guard (checksum recheck of the recorded workflow_file, then audit) right before the prologue, via StateManager.record_workflow_checksum_mismatch / record_resume_projection_integrity_failure (raw-JSON, three-field delta). Child frame executors skip it. Sticky handling: _execute_call notes the diagnostic as run error, _handle_control_flow returns "_stop" ahead of routes/on_error, for_each stops iterating, repeat_until frame carries the unwrapped diagnostic, finalization records supplemental failure (error null for ordinary cleanup failure) and never replaces the run error.
- calls.py: resume path resolves the reached boundary once (boundary alias selects the callee), revalidates the boundary's frames, rejects completed-frame id collisions before grouping, selects the frame by lineage (no mapping order), runs checksum / bound-input validation, then audits failed predecessors (checksum first) and the running member with audit_scope before any child manager exists. Projection failures are returned unwrapped (never call_failed). _is_workflow_lisp_target now means frontend_kind == "workflow_lisp".
- Delegated and reviewed: duplicate classic-YAML import aliases (loader_import_aliases.py, compose-time check before bundle construction), frontend_kind plumbed through elaborate_surface_workflow and build_frontend_bundle no longer overwriting it, state recorders, forensic current_step handling in observability report/monitor (I added the dashboard guard), and specs/state.md + specs/acceptance/index.md (I added two clarifying lines) plus a short docs/plans note.
- Tests: new tests/test_resume_projection_integrity.py, _runtime.py, test_resume_projection_failure_envelopes.py, test_import_alias_duplicates_and_frontend_provenance.py; the old characterization tests that froze the gaps (mapping-order frame pick, stale caller starts a fresh child, resume_state_integrity_error for current_step, observability-before-audit ordering) were rewritten to the new contract.
- Verification: narrow suites, collect-only, a CLI smoke (stale steps.<name>.step_id -> exit 1, stderr reason, only status/error/updated_at changed, report shows the diagnostic), and the full pytest -n 16 run: 47 failures, all of which also fail on a clean export of HEAD (48 there); no new failures.

ALTERNATIVES / DECISIONS
- Considered checksumming the bundle's provenance path in the executor guard (as call frames do); dropped it because tests compile bundles from a copy, so the recorded workflow_file (as StateManager.initialize used) is the authoritative file.
- Considered putting max_iterations on IterationStepKeyProjection; dropped to keep serialized projection goldens stable. Only import_alias needed golden updates (two files).
- Considered auditing the parent scope again at every reached call; dropped because the one-resolve_call_boundary-per-reached-identity rule would break, so a reached call revalidates only its own boundary's frames and the callee scope.
- A terminal exhausted repeat_until whose loop row is absent is accepted (lexical restore deliberately pops it); a present row must match.
- Several judgement calls where the brief is silent: ambiguous step candidates report presentation_slot_mismatch; an out-of-range for_each current_index reuses the completed_indices out-of-range message; stale/unowned for_each/repeat_until bookkeeping names report invalid_loop_progress; step rows are checked before current_step before call frames, and loop bookkeeping errors (needed to build the index) come first; expected_owner.workflow_file is the bundle's provenance workflow path; CLI prints a Field: line after the error.

WHAT I DID NOT COVER
- Existing fixtures changed because the contract requires it: current_step.step_id is now mandatory, root executor resumes recheck the checksum, Workflow Lisp compiler bundles now take the Lisp default-resume route (pure-projection tests needed a legacy lowering context), adjudication changed_candidate_config now stops at the checksum guard. Hidden tests that assume the old behaviour will differ.
- Frame-level 'current position' mandatory checks are only covered through the callee scope audit.
- No tmux/orchestrator workflow smoke beyond the resume CLI; nothing committed. docs/index.md and the capability matrix were left alone (live selector wording is yours).
- Cyclomatic complexity was only estimated by a script (no radon); pre-existing calls.py functions remain over 12.
value.summary: Resume now audits every persisted identity (steps, current step, loops, call frames, Workflow Lisp retry lineage) against the current projection at the CLI, at the root executor and at each reached call, failing closed with a sticky, privacy-bounded resume_projection_integrity_error; the other pieces are in too and the full suite shows no new failures against HEAD.
